So I've tried Hearthstone a few times and tend to enjoy it but it hasn't held my interest for long enough in the past. I'm trying to get into it a bit more properly now that I have some free time. I don't plan on spending money on the game, other than probably buying the expansion packs if I find myself interested enough.

I've been trying to level up all the classes to lvl 10 as I think that's a good thing to do as a new player and have a couple of questions:

  1. Are there 'better' classes for new players to learn with? I've tried googling but tend to find 'Beginner Builds' for all the classes (which is fine). Just wondering if there's one I should focus on? And at that, are there more difficult classes that are harder to master?

  2. Should I be focusing on a specific class? I get the impression that I'm going to have to craft good cards if I want to make a really competitive deck and to do that I might need to pick a specific class to focus on. Is that a good idea, or should I pick a couple or ?

  3. Guides I've read have said to just focus on 'Arena' rather than buying packs, which I completely understand. Is there a point at which I should start crafting more and looking to play other game types?
A few questions from a Beginner

While I've been playing since the beginning, I'm very much a casual so take this for what it's worth. There are better players out there and it's your time and money so do what you like.

  1. I've actually found all of the classes to be fun if you give them a try. Depending on how much time you want to give to the game, it's very helpful to play all of the classes because you will be facing all of them. It helps to understand what their hero power does and what cards they have available to them. hearthpwn.com is one of the better spots to learn how to build a deck for a class you are interested in, but don't get discouraged if a lot of the decks are using cards you do not have access to yet. When I started, I tended toward the classes that I played in WoW predominantly, but there's really no rhyme or reason to it. Just play what you like and feel free to experiment. While there are serious players out there, the real fun is to experiment with all sorts of silly builds. Winning on a silly build is so much more fun than just mindlessly netdecking the latest and greatest.

  2. Competitive deck buiding is interesting. You are always looking for that advantage from a better deck and that's what keeps us coming back. However, some of the best players are using decks that don't have a lot of expensive cards in them. One of my favorite decks has no epics or legendaries in it. As for fixating on one class and wearing it out, you can do that if you like but you may burn out on playing it if you only do one class all of the time. I started with the hunter and got really sick of it and was always jealous of the spells that another class had. Then one day I remembered, I can play that class if I want (and then got promptly owned by a hunter so go figure). Also, Blizzard is tweaking the balance so your favorite OP deck today may be disenchantment dust tomorrow.

  3. Arena can be fun, but it's a matter of how well you are going to do in arena (and I'm not that great). I think that some of the players prefer arena because you theoretically have access to a random assortment of all of the cards and it's a lot of fun to play strange combinations that are difficult or impossible to have in your other decks.

My humble recommendation is to play the style you like and not worry too much about power gaming this game. It's a casual game despite of how serious some people make it. If you like the solo campaign stuff, the Naxx and Blackrock mountain bosses are seriously fun and their heroic modes can provide hours of entertainment. Also, these two campaigns are going to lead to more legendary cards than a lot of arenas or packs. If you like ranked play, do it. If you like arenas, do that. If your goal is to get packs faster, remember that it costs 150 gold to do arena and 100 gold to buy a pack. If you don't win at least a couple of times in arena, the buying of the pack is a better back for your gold.

Please fight the urge to buy arenas or packs or skins or whatever with real cash. There is a real tendency to play another player, get completely wiped out by a legendary card and think "if I only had that card I'd rock." While I appreciate those players spending all of that real cash to keep the game going, I really recommend you live off of gold purchases for a bit because it means you are only dealing with learning a few cards at a time. No matter what cards you have, you'll hit players with very common decks who are simply more skillful.

As for crafting, I'd recommend collecting dust for a bit. If you find a deck that you like and wish you just had that one more card, it's your dust and you can craft it. But every time I do that, I end up getting that card within a few packs. I'm sure it's just confirmation bias, but it seems to go that way and it makes me chuckle every time.
